Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

For positive semidefinite matrices $A$ and $B$, Ando and Zhan proved the inequalities $||| f(A)+f(B) ||| \ge ||| f(A+B) |||$ and $||| g(A)+g(B) ||| \le ||| g(A+B) |||$, for any unitarily invariant norm, and for any non-negative operator monotone $f$ on $[0,\infty)$ with inverse function $g$. These inequalities have very recently been generalised to non-negative concave functions $f$ and non-negative convex functions $g$, by Bourin and Uchiyama, and Kosem, respectively.   In this paper we consider the related question whether the inequalities $||| f(A)-f(B) ||| \le ||| f(|A-B|) |||$, and $||| g(A)-g(B) ||| \ge ||| g(|A-B|) |||$, obtained by Ando, for operator monotone $f$ with inverse $g$, also have a similar generalisation to non-negative concave $f$ and convex $g$. We answer exactly this question, in the negative for general matrices, and affirmatively in the special case when $A\ge ||B||$.   In the course of this work, we introduce the novel notion of $Y$-dominated majorisation between the spectra of two Hermitian matrices, where $Y$ is itself a Hermitian matrix, and prove a certain property of this relation that allows to strengthen the results of Bourin-Uchiyama and Kosem, mentioned above.

For positive semidefinite matrices \(A\) and \(B\), Ando and Zhan proved the inequalities
\[
||| f(A)+f(B) ||| \ge ||| f(A+B) |||
\quad \text{and} \quad
||| g(A)+g(B) ||| \le ||| g(A+B) |||,
\]
for every unitarily invariant norm, and for every non-negative operator monotone function \(f\) on \([0,\infty)\) with inverse function \(g\). These inequalities have very recently been generalised to non-negative concave functions \(f\) and non-negative convex functions \(g\) by Bourin and Uchiyama, and by Kosem, respectively.

In this paper, we consider the related question of whether the inequalities
\[
||| f(A)-f(B) ||| \le ||| f(|A-B|) |||
\quad \text{and} \quad
||| g(A)-g(B) ||| \ge ||| g(|A-B|) |||,
\]
obtained by Ando for operator monotone \(f\) with inverse \(g\), admit a similar generalisation to non-negative concave functions \(f\) and convex functions \(g\). We answer this question precisely: in the negative for general matrices, and affirmatively in the special case where \(A \ge ||B||\).

In the course of this work, we introduce the novel notion of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation between the spectra of two Hermitian matrices, where \(Y\) is itself a Hermitian matrix. We also prove a certain property of this relation that makes it possible to strengthen the aforementioned results of Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem.

Ando and Zhan established that, for positive semidefinite matrices \(A\) and \(B\), the inequalities
\[
|||f(A)+f(B)||| \ge |||f(A+B)|||
\]
and
\[
|||g(A)+g(B)||| \le |||g(A+B)|||
\]
hold for every unitarily invariant norm, whenever \(f\) is a non-negative operator monotone function on \([0,\infty)\) and \(g\) is its inverse. More recently, these results were extended: Bourin and Uchiyama proved the corresponding statement for non-negative concave functions \(f\), while Kosem did so for non-negative convex functions \(g\).

This paper investigates a closely connected problem: whether Ando’s inequalities
\[
|||f(A)-f(B)||| \le |||f(|A-B|)|||
\]
and
\[
|||g(A)-g(B)||| \ge |||g(|A-B|)|||
\]
originally obtained for operator monotone \(f\) with inverse \(g\), admit analogous extensions to the broader classes of non-negative concave functions \(f\) and non-negative convex functions \(g\). We show that, for arbitrary matrices, such an extension is not possible, but that it does hold in the particular situation where \(A \ge \|B\|\).

As part of the analysis, we also define a new concept: \(Y\)-dominated majorisation between the spectra of two Hermitian matrices, with \(Y\) itself Hermitian. We prove a property of this relation which, in turn, yields strengthened versions of the previously mentioned results of Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem.
outputs.L3:
Ando and Zhan established important norm inequalities for positive semidefinite matrices involving operator monotone functions and their inverse functions. Their results apply under arbitrary unitarily invariant norms and provide a powerful framework for comparing matrix expressions of the form involving sums of positive semidefinite matrices and the corresponding sums of their images under suitable functions.

More recently, Bourin, Uchiyama, and Kosem extended these inequalities beyond the setting of operator monotone functions. They showed that analogous norm inequalities remain valid for broader classes of scalar functions, namely non-negative concave functions and non-negative convex functions. This generalization is significant because concavity and convexity are much less restrictive assumptions than operator monotonicity, and therefore the resulting inequalities apply to a wider range of matrix functions.

The paper in question examines whether similar generalizations are possible for inequalities involving differences of matrix functions. In particular, it asks whether known difference inequalities, originally proved for operator monotone functions, continue to hold when the function is merely non-negative and concave, or when its inverse-type counterpart is non-negative and convex. Such inequalities are more delicate than inequalities for sums, because differences of positive semidefinite matrices need not preserve positivity in the same robust way.

The authors show that, in general, these difference inequalities cannot be extended to arbitrary matrices under the broader assumptions of concavity or convexity. Thus, the direct analogue of the Ando–Zhan type results for differences fails in the general matrix setting. However, they also identify an important special case in which the inequalities do remain valid: when the positive semidefinite matrix \(A\) dominates the norm of \(B\), that is, when  
\[
A \geq \|B\|.
\]
Under this additional hypothesis, the desired norm inequalities for differences of matrix functions can be established even for the wider classes of non-negative concave and convex functions.

A further contribution of the paper is the introduction of the notion of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation between spectra of Hermitian matrices. This concept provides a refined way of comparing eigenvalue distributions while taking into account domination by an auxiliary matrix \(Y\). Using this new form of majorisation, the authors strengthen earlier results due to Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem. In particular, their approach yields sharper spectral comparisons and provides a deeper explanation for why certain norm inequalities extend from operator monotone functions to the broader concave and convex settings, while others require additional structural assumptions.
outputs.L4:
This paper studies extensions of Ando’s norm inequalities for differences of positive semidefinite matrices. Ando’s original results show that, for suitable operator monotone functions, certain unitarily invariant norm inequalities hold when such functions are applied to positive semidefinite matrices. A natural question is whether these inequalities remain valid for a wider class of scalar functions, in particular for arbitrary non-negative concave functions and for convex functions of inverse type.

The paper shows that, in full generality, these extensions are false. Although concavity is often sufficient for many trace and norm inequalities involving positive operators, it does not by itself guarantee the validity of Ando-type inequalities for matrix differences. Counterexamples demonstrate that replacing operator monotonicity by ordinary concavity can fail when the matrices involved are arbitrary positive semidefinite matrices.

However, the paper identifies an important setting in which the desired inequalities do remain true. If the positive semidefinite matrices \(A\) and \(B\) satisfy the additional domination condition
\[
A \geq \|B\|,
\]
then Ando-type inequalities can be extended beyond operator monotone functions. Under this hypothesis, the relevant inequalities hold for all non-negative concave functions, and analogous results are obtained for appropriate convex inverse-type functions. Thus, while the general extension is impossible, the paper gives a sharp positive result under a natural spectral dominance assumption.

A central tool in the argument is spectral majorisation. The paper develops and uses a new form of majorisation, called \(Y\)-dominated majorisation, designed to compare spectra in situations where ordinary majorisation is too weak or too rigid. This notion makes it possible to control eigenvalue distributions of matrix differences after applying concave or convex functions. It provides a refined framework for proving norm inequalities for positive semidefinite matrices and their functional transforms.

The introduction of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation also yields improvements to known results. In particular, the paper strengthens related inequalities due to Bourin and Uchiyama, as well as results of Kosem. These earlier works established important norm and majorisation inequalities for concave functions of positive operators. By applying the new majorisation method, the paper obtains sharper or more general versions of these results, clarifying the role of spectral domination in such inequalities.

Overall, the paper gives a precise answer to the question of how far Ando’s inequalities can be extended. It shows that operator monotonicity cannot simply be replaced by scalar concavity in the general matrix setting, but that meaningful extensions are possible under the condition \(A \geq \|B\|\). The new concept of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation serves as the main technical innovation and provides a useful tool for further study of eigenvalue and norm inequalities involving positive semidefinite matrices.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a mathematical research paper on extending Ando's norm inequalities for positive semidefinite matrices from operator monotone functions to general concave/convex functions, including negative results and a special affirmative case.
counterfactuals.output:
We investigate the extent to which Ando-type norm inequalities for positive semidefinite matrices remain valid when the underlying operator monotone functions are replaced by general scalar concave or convex functions. Classical results assert that, for suitable operator monotone functions and unitarily invariant norms, inequalities comparing functions of sums, compressions, and congruences hold in strong matrix-norm form. It is natural to ask whether operator monotonicity can be weakened to ordinary concavity or convexity.

We show that, in general, such extensions fail. In particular, we construct counterexamples demonstrating that scalar concavity alone does not preserve the relevant unitarily invariant norm inequalities, even for positive semidefinite matrices of small size. Analogous negative results are obtained in the convex setting, showing that the expected reversed inequalities also do not hold without additional structural assumptions. These examples clarify the essential role played by operator monotonicity in Ando’s original framework.

On the positive side, we identify a special affirmative case in which an Ando-type inequality survives beyond the operator monotone class. Specifically, for a restricted family of concave/convex functions and matrix configurations, the desired norm comparison follows from majorization arguments and spectral estimates. This result delineates a precise boundary between purely scalar functional properties and genuinely operator-theoretic monotonicity. Together, the negative and positive results provide a sharper understanding of the limitations and possible extensions of Ando’s norm inequalities for positive semidefinite matrices.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main results of a paper about unitarily invariant norm inequalities involving \(f(A)-f(B)\), \(g(A)-g(B)\), and \(f(|A-B|)\), referencing Ando-Zhan, Bourin-Uchiyama, and Kosem.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper’s main theme is a Lipschitz-type inequality for functions of positive semidefinite matrices measured in arbitrary unitarily invariant norms.  It fits into a line of results initiated by Ando–Zhan and Bourin–Uchiyama and connected with a conjecture/result of Kosem.

For positive semidefinite matrices \(A,B\) and a unitarily invariant norm \(\|\!\|\cdot\|\!\|\), the central inequality is of the form

\[
\bigl\|\, f(A)-f(B)\,\bigr\| \leq 
\bigl\|\, f(|A-B|)\,\bigr\|,
\]

where \(f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is concave, typically with \(f(0)=0\), and \(|A-B|\) denotes the positive square root of \((A-B)^2\).

### Main results

1. **Extension of the Ando–Zhan inequality.**  
   Ando and Zhan had proved the above inequality for nonnegative operator monotone functions \(f\). Since operator monotone functions on \([0,\infty)\) are concave, the natural question was whether operator monotonicity could be weakened to mere concavity. The paper confirms this broader concave-function version, establishing

   \[
   \bigl\|\, f(A)-f(B)\,\bigr\|
   \leq
   \bigl\|\, f(|A-B|)\,\bigr\|
   \]

   for every unitarily invariant norm.

2. **Resolution/confirmation of Kosem’s conjecture.**  
   Kosem had considered precisely this strengthening from operator monotone functions to general nonnegative concave functions. The paper proves the expected inequality in full generality, thereby settling Kosem’s problem.

3. **Comparison principle involving two functions \(f\) and \(g\).**  
   A more general result is proved for two functions \(f\) and \(g\). Roughly, if \(f\) and \(g\) are nonnegative concave functions and one has a pointwise domination relation such as

   \[
   f(t)\leq g(t) \qquad (t\geq 0),
   \]

   then the corresponding matrix differences satisfy a norm comparison

   \[
   \bigl\|\, f(A)-f(B)\,\bigr\|
   \leq
   \bigl\|\, g(A)-g(B)\,\bigr\|
   \]

   under the appropriate hypotheses. This shows that the size of \(f(A)-f(B)\) in any unitarily invariant norm is controlled by the scalar behavior of \(f\).

4. **Use of Bourin–Uchiyama subadditivity techniques.**  
   Bourin and Uchiyama had proved important norm inequalities for concave functions, especially subadditivity-type results such as

   \[
   \bigl\|\, f(A+B)\,\bigr\|
   \leq
   \bigl\|\, f(A)+f(B)\,\bigr\|
   \]

   for positive semidefinite \(A,B\) and concave \(f\geq0\). The paper relies on and extends these ideas to handle differences \(f(A)-f(B)\), which are more delicate because they need not be positive.

5. **Sharp norm inequality for perturbations.**  
   The inequality

   \[
   \bigl\|\, f(A)-f(B)\,\bigr\|
   \leq
   \bigl\|\, f(|A-B|)\,\bigr\|
   \]

   can be interpreted as saying that applying a nonnegative concave function to positive matrices is norm-contracting with respect to the perturbation \(A-B\), after the perturbation is transformed by the same function \(f\). In particular, for functions such as \(f(t)=t^\alpha\), \(0\leq \alpha\leq1\), one obtains

   \[
   \bigl\|\, A^\alpha-B^\alpha\,\bigr\|
   \leq
   \bigl\|\, |A-B|^\alpha\,\bigr\|.
   \]

### Overall significance

The paper strengthens the Ando–Zhan theorem by replacing operator monotonicity with ordinary concavity, confirms the inequality anticipated by Kosem, and places the result within the broader Bourin–Uchiyama framework of unitarily invariant norm inequalities for concave functions of matrices. Its main contribution is showing that for positive matrices, the norm of the difference \(f(A)-f(B)\) is universally bounded by the norm of \(f(|A-B|)\), for all unitarily invariant norms.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a formal journal-style abstract for a matrix analysis paper that investigates whether Ando’s inequalities for operator monotone functions and their inverses generalize to non-negative concave and convex functions.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract.**  
Ando’s inequalities provide fundamental comparisons for positive linear maps and operator monotone functions, together with corresponding inverse forms that play an important role in matrix analysis and operator theory. In this paper we examine whether these inequalities persist when the operator monotonicity hypothesis is replaced by the weaker assumptions of non-negativity and scalar concavity or convexity. We show that, in general, such extensions fail. By constructing explicit finite-dimensional counterexamples, we demonstrate that non-negative concave functions need not satisfy the Ando-type inequalities valid for operator monotone functions, and that analogous inverse inequalities cannot be recovered under mere convexity assumptions. The results clarify the essential role of operator monotonicity in Ando’s framework and delineate the limitations of extending operator inequalities from the operator-monotone setting to broader classes of scalar functions. Our analysis also identifies structural obstructions arising from the noncommutative order and highlights the distinction between scalar Jensen-type behavior and matrix order preservation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a concise academic abstract describing new results on inequalities for positive semidefinite matrices, including counterexamples for general matrices, a positive result when \(A \ge \|B\|\), and a new concept called \(Y\)-dominated majorisation.
counterfactuals.output: We establish new inequalities for positive semidefinite matrices and clarify the extent to which they fail beyond the positive setting. In particular, we show that several natural norm and eigenvalue inequalities, valid under positivity assumptions, admit counterexamples for arbitrary matrices, demonstrating that no direct extension to the general case is possible without additional hypotheses. As a positive result, we prove that the desired comparison remains valid when the positive semidefinite matrix \(A\) dominates the perturbation size, namely under the condition \(A \ge \|B\| I\). This yields a robust sufficient criterion ensuring the preservation of the relevant spectral inequalities. We also introduce a refinement of classical majorisation, termed \(Y\)-dominated majorisation, designed to encode spectral domination relative to a fixed positive semidefinite matrix \(Y\). This framework provides a unified language for the new inequalities and suggests further applications to matrix analysis, operator inequalities, and perturbation theory.

counterfactuals.prompt: Given a paper proving limitations and extensions of Ando-type inequalities for unitarily invariant norms and introducing \(Y\)-dominated majorisation of Hermitian spectra, generate a polished abstract in the style of a mathematics journal.
counterfactuals.output:
We investigate the scope of Ando-type inequalities for unitarily invariant norms and identify structural obstructions to several natural extensions. In particular, we show that inequalities which hold in the positive semidefinite setting need not persist under more general Hermitian perturbations or under naive spectral domination hypotheses. To formulate sharp replacements, we introduce a notion of \(Y\)-dominated majorisation for Hermitian spectra, designed to encode the interaction between eigenvalue ordering and a fixed comparison operator \(Y\).

This majorisation relation provides a flexible framework for comparing spectral data beyond the classical positive cone and yields new sufficient conditions under which Ando-type norm inequalities remain valid for all unitarily invariant norms. We establish its basic properties, relate it to standard weak majorisation and Ky Fan norm inequalities, and show how it captures precisely the additional information needed in several borderline cases. The resulting theorems both clarify the limitations of existing Ando inequalities and furnish extensions applicable to broader classes of Hermitian matrices and operator expressions.
